questions.skill: Explain similarity of triangles as equal angles and proportional sides
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A similarity transformation (a dilation with scale factor k followed by rigid motions) maps △ABC onto △DEF with A → D, B → E, C → F. Explain why ∠A ≅ ∠D, ∠B ≅ ∠E, ∠C ≅ ∠F and DE/AB = EF/BC = FD/CA = k.
questions.prompt_markup: A similarity transformation (a dilation with scale factor k followed by rigid motions) maps △ABC onto △DEF with A → D, B → E, C → F. Explain why ∠A ≅ ∠D, ∠B ≅ ∠E, ∠C ≅ ∠F and DE/AB = EF/BC = FD/CA = k.
questions.correct_answer: Angles are preserved and every length is multiplied by k.
questions.required_method: Use what dilations and rigid motions do to angles and to lengths.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: dilations and rigid motions preserve angle measure, so corresponding angles are congruent; the dilation multiplies every length by k and rigid motions keep lengths, so each image side is k times its original side.

questions.correct_answer: No. XY/AB = 1.5 and YZ/BC = 1.5 but ZX/CA = 1.25; similar triangles need all three ratios equal (one scale factor).
